business.title: Fatty acid 2-hydroxylation restrains gastric cancer by blocking CD36 palmitoylation and fatty acid uptake
business.description: Fatty acid (FA)-induced internalization of the FA transporter CD36 normally functions as an intrinsic brake on FA uptake and lipid overload, but cancer cells can bypass this checkpoint to sustain lipid-fueled growth. The mechanism underlying this failure remains unclear. Here, we identify a FA 2-hydroxylase (FA2H)-CD36 signaling axis that operates as an endogenous brake on lipid fueling in gastric cancer cells. FA2H-derived (R)-2-hydroxy palmitic acid ((R)-2-OHPA) disrupts CD36 interaction with its palmitoyltransferase DHHC4, thereby limiting CD36 palmitoylation and trafficking to the plasma membrane. Loss of FA2H permits CD36 palmitoylation and establishes a feed-forward loop that amplifies FA uptake, lipid accumulation, and tumor growth. Restoring FA2H expression or supplementing cells with exogenous (R)-2-OHPA reinstates the lipid-sensing checkpoint. Moreover, FA2H activation sensitizes gastric cancer cells to inhibition of endogenous FA synthesis through blockade of FA synthase (FASN) or stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD1). In vivo, (R)-2-OHPA treatment or expression of the palmitoylation-deficient CD36 AASS mutant attenuates FA2H deficiency-driven lipid accumulation and tumor growth, positioning CD36 palmitoylation as the critical effector in this metabolic circuit. Together, these findings establish FA 2-hydroxylation as a metabolic checkpoint that links FA structure to CD36 trafficking and FA utilization in gastric cancer, revealing a targetable vulnerability in lipid-driven tumor growth.

science.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based diagnostic model for depression in young populations: a retrospective cohort study
science.description: Depression in 10–26 years is often subtle but can greatly affect their physical and mental development. This study aims to develop a machine learning model for the diagnosis of depression. Data were collected from 600 patients aged 10–26 years between 2019 and 2025, including 350 non-depressed patients and 250 depressed patients. A gradient boosting machine (GBM) was used to build the model, shapley additive explanations (SHAP) plots employed for model interpretation and visualization. Based on Boruta feature selection, nine variables were identified for machine learning model construction: S100β, platelet(PLT), lactate dehydrogenase(LDH), white blood cell(WBC), creatinine kinase-mb(CK-Mb), gender, and LDH/PLT Ratio, LDH/WBC Ratio, LDH/HGB Ratio. The GBM showed the best performance with a threshold of 0.591, Accuracy of 0.878, Specificity of 0.941, and Precision of 0.913. It also demonstrated high levels of Sensitivity (0.797) and F1 Score (0.851). The decision curve analysis and calibration curve assessed the clinical validity and consistency of the model, indicating that the GBM model outperformed others. The most significant features identified were S100β, PLT, and LDH/PLT. By utilizing machine learning, key factors such as S100β, PLT, and LDH/PLT were identified, providing preliminary evidence for the diagnosis of depression in patients aged 10–26 years.

science.title: Hybrid optimization of multimodal SLAM for underground robots with seismic vibration geomagnetic and tactile sensing
science.description: Reliable underground SLAM remains difficult when GPS, visual features, LiDAR, or external anchors are unavailable or degraded, while non-visual sensors exhibit noise, drift, and environment-dependent uncertainty. We propose a hybrid-optimized seismic/vibration-geomagnetic-tactile SLAM framework that combines complementary sensor factors in a robust factor graph and uses staged COA-PSO-GSA optimization for automated parameter calibration. Evaluation covered 23 complete trajectories (10.2 km; approximately 7.5 h) from simulation, controlled underground corridors, and field tunnel/mine environments, with non-overlapping trajectory-level optimization, validation, and testing subsets. On the test trajectories, mean absolute trajectory error was 0.53 m, convergence occurred in approximately 37 iterations, and error growth remained between 1.81% and 4.09% under the evaluated magnetic, vibration, and tactile degradation conditions. Loop-detection AUC was 0.76, but its difference from the strongest GWO-SLAM baseline (0.74) was not statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.184). The measured foreground update latency was 57 ± 10 ms (approximately 17.5 Hz), indicating near-real-time online operation on the tested platform rather than hard real-time performance. These results support technical feasibility under the tested conditions, while broader claims require larger multi-site validation.

science.title: Antibacterial activity of ferrocene-derived multi-walled carbon nanotubes synthesized by chemical vapor deposition against Escherichia coli
science.description: Multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were synthesized by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) using ferrocene as the carbon and iron-catalyst precursor and were evaluated for antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli ATCC 25,922. The as-grown material was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The characterization results confirmed the formation of graphitized multi-walled nanotube structures and the presence of iron-containing residues derived from the ferrocene precursor. Antibacterial activity was assessed by agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and viable-count plating. A concentration-dependent reduction in bacterial growth was observed over the tested range of 1–512 µg/mL. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined to be 256 µg/mL based on the absence of visible bacterial growth, with blank-corrected quantitative measurements providing supplementary confirmation of the inhibitory endpoint. Viable-count analysis on drug-free Mueller–Hinton agar showed no recoverable colonies at 256 and 512 µg/mL, supporting a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 256 µg/mL under the experimental conditions. In the agar well-diffusion assay, inhibition-zone diameters were 26, 21, 19, 9, and 7 mm at 512, 256, 128, 64, and 32 µg/mL, respectively, whereas no inhibition was observed in the negative control. These findings demonstrate concentration-dependent antibacterial activity of the as-grown ferrocene-derived MWCNT preparation against E. coli ATCC 25,922. Because the material was evaluated without post-synthesis purification, the observed activity represents the response to the as-grown preparation, including potential contributions from synthesis-derived components.

science.title: Effect of occlusal loading and crown material on stress and strain distribution in bone around 4-mm ultra-short implants: a 3D-FEA
science.description: Ultra-short (4-mm) dental implants represent a minimally invasive solution for the rehabilitation of posterior atrophic regions; however, concerns remain regarding stress and strain concentration in bone around implants under functional loading. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of occlusal loading conditions, prosthetic configuration, and crown material on stress and strain distribution using three-dimensional finite element analysis (3D-FEA). Three-dimensional finite element models of single-crown restorations and the splinted two-crown configuration supported by 4-mm ultra-short implants were developed. Zirconia and composite resin crowns were evaluated under vertical and 30° oblique loading, with and without a simulated food bolus. The bolus was assigned a Young’s modulus of 10 MPa and a Poisson’s ratio of 0.30. Primary outcomes were volume-weighted mean von Mises stress and equivalent elastic strain within a fixed 0.50-mm peri-implant volumetric region of interest (ROI). Mesh convergence was assessed using three nominal local refinement levels and a 5% acceptance threshold. In single-crown models without bolus, oblique loading increased cortical ROI stress from approximately 10.01 to 43.02 MPa and trabecular ROI stress from approximately 4.95 to 12.35 MPa. With bolus interposition, corresponding oblique values decreased to approximately 19.57 and 5.63 MPa. In models of the splinted two-crown configuration, cortical ROI stress under oblique loading ranged from 8.63 to 10.43 MPa. Zirconia and composite resin produced nearly identical ROI outcomes in the single-crown configurations, whereas a modest configuration-specific difference was observed under oblique loading in the splinted two-crown configuration. All primary outcomes met the 5% convergence criterion. Within the assumptions of this finite element model, loading direction and prosthetic configuration had greater effects on peri-implant stress and strain than crown material. Bolus interposition reduced the ROI outcomes under oblique loading. Under the modeled oblique conditions, the splinted two-crown configuration was associated with lower peri-implant ROI outcomes than the single-crown configuration; however, the different total loads prevent isolation of splinting as an independent causal factor. These comparative findings do not establish clinical superiority or biomechanical reliability and require experimental and clinical validation.

science.title: Co-inoculation with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens enhances the fermentation quality and in vitro ruminal digestibility of whole-plant millet silage
science.description: Whole-plant millet is a climate-resilient alternative forage requiring ensiling optimization. This study evaluated single and combined bacterial inoculants on the fermentation quality and in vitro ruminal degradability of millet silage. Forage harvested at the grain-filling stage was ensiled for 60 days with sterile water (Negative Control), Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (L), Lactobacillus mucosae (M), or their combinations with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (LB, MB) at 1 × 106 colony-forming units/g fresh matter, followed by a 72-h in vitro rumen assay. Compared with the control, bacterial inoculation significantly reduced silage pH (4.876 vs. 4.683–4.788, P < 0.001) and increased lactic acid concentration (2.543 vs. 2.938–3.450% of dry matter, P < 0.001) after 60 d ensiling. Inoculated silages also showed lower ammonia nitrogen concentrations (4.731 vs. 3.868–4.055 mg/dL, P < 0.001) and reduced neutral detergent fiber contents (59.675 vs. 58.213–58.574% of dry matter, P < 0.001). Consequently, inoculated silages yielded higher in vitro dry matter and fiber digestibility, alongside elevated volatile fatty acid concentrations. Notably, co-inoculating L. plantarum and B. amyloliquefaciens exhibited greatest fermentation efficiency, showing the highest asymptotic gas production and average gas production rate (AGPR) among all treatments (P < 0.05). While a transient reduction in the proportion of ruminal methane occurred during early incubation (24–48 h, P < 0.05), it was not sustained by 72 h. Overall, multispecies bacterial inoculation improves the fermentative efficiency and nutritional degradability of whole-plant millet silage, optimizing sustainable roughage resources.
